title: KOSPI Close November 3, 2026: Falls 3.59% to 5,648.79, KOSDAQ -4.08%
content:
KOSPI closed at 5,648.79, down 3.59%, and KOSDAQ closed at 704.39, down 4.08%, as weakness in U.S. tech stocks and renewed worries about the profitability of AI infrastructure spending hit large chip stocks. Against the sell-off, individual themes moved on their own news: Hanjin Group affiliates on a control contest over Hanjin KAL, space and satellite stocks, information security stocks after a string of financial-sector data leaks, and an AI regenerative medicine name.

1. Sharp drop — U.S. tech weakness and AI spending worries

After a rebound the previous day, Korean stocks opened lower as U.S. tech weakness and doubts about the profitability of AI infrastructure investment returned. In the U.S., concern about the investment burden grew after Oracle announced a plan to raise $20 billion to fund AI infrastructure, and chip stocks such as Intel and AMD also fell.

In Korea, selling centered on large chip stocks such as Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, and the decline widened to chip equipment, materials and parts makers and to secondary battery stocks.

2. Hoban Group vs. Cho Won-tae — control contest at Hanjin KAL

Hanjin Group related stocks, including Hanjin KAL preferred shares, Hanjin KAL, Hanjin and Asiana IDT, rose sharply together.

It became known that Hoban Group had secured an additional stake in Hanjin KAL and applied to the Fair Trade Commission for a business combination review. Chairman Cho Won-tae of Hanjin Group was also reported to have signed a contract to buy about 37.05 billion won of Hanjin KAL shares: 325,000 common shares at 114,000 won each, to be bought through after-hours block trades from December 3 to January 1. With Hoban's larger stake and Cho's response overlapping, the possibility of a change in Hanjin KAL's governance and a contest for control drew attention.

3. Space and satellite stocks — delivery for Korea's navigation satellite system

  • AP Satellite: completed delivery of AVTS, test and verification equipment for satellites of the Korea Positioning System (KPS), to the Korea Aerospace Research Institute. AVTS checks the electrical and electronic signals of a satellite's flight module from the ground and verifies that it works normally. It is the company's first AVTS supply record, and it hopes for more equipment supply in follow-up KPS satellite projects.
  • Contec and LK Samyang: grouped into the same theme.

KPS is a national space project worth about 3.7235 trillion won, building a total of eight navigation satellites by 2035. The first satellite is targeted for launch in September 2029, which also fed expectations of longer-term demand for satellite parts and equipment.

4. Information security stocks — leaks at financial firms

Hansak, S2W, Pescaro, CyberOne, Genians, AhnLab, Fasoo AI and Intellivix were strong as hacking and personal data leaks kept occurring, mainly in the financial sector.

A customer data leak occurred at Daishin Securities, and unauthorized external access was confirmed at Mirae Asset Global Investments and at the crypto exchange Bithumb. On November 3, a leak of customer and employee personal data through an external groupware system was confirmed at Hanyang Securities, raising wariness about security incidents in finance further.

  • Hansak: network security and data transfer solutions, with expectations of stronger network security at financial institutions.
  • Fasoo AI: document and data security, privacy protection and AI data security.
  • S2W: cyber threat intelligence and big data analysis, for detecting and responding to hacking threats.
  • Pescaro: automotive software and vehicle cybersecurity.
  • CyberOne: information security consulting, security monitoring and vulnerability assessment.
  • Genians: network access control (NAC) and endpoint detection and response (EDR).
  • AhnLab: antivirus, endpoint and network security, a leading name in the theme.
  • Intellivix: AI video analytics and intelligent CCTV, so its move reflects physical security and video monitoring as well as information security.

5. AI regenerative medicine — China entry and medical device exports

Rokit Healthcare uses AI-based customized 3D bioprinting for skin regeneration and chronic wound treatment. It plans to start exporting medical devices and skin regeneration kits to China in earnest from December, and to attend an international medical device expo in Hainan, China, to present its AI skin regeneration platform and local commercialization strategy. It is also working toward a first skin regeneration procedure at Hainan Boao Super Hospital in January, and the stock appears to reflect hopes that the China push could turn into actual sales.

Quick FAQ

How did KOSPI and KOSDAQ close on Nov 3?
KOSPI fell 3.59% to 5,648.79 and KOSDAQ fell 4.08% to 704.39. U.S. tech weakness and AI spending worries drove selling in Samsung Electronics, SK hynix and other large chip stocks.

Why did Hanjin Group stocks surge?
Hoban Group's additional stake in Hanjin KAL and its merger review filing became known, and Chairman Cho Won-tae was reported to have signed a contract to buy about 37.05 billion won of Hanjin KAL shares, raising the possibility of a control contest.

Why were security stocks strong?
Data leaks were confirmed at Daishin Securities, Mirae Asset Global Investments, Bithumb and, on Nov 3, Hanyang Securities, which raised the need for stronger information security.
